content:
The prime factorization of \(17017\) is \(7 \times 11 \times 13 \times 17\). Therefore,

\[
17017^{17} = 7^{17} \times 11^{17} \times 13^{17} \times 17^{17}.
\]

A divisor \(d\) of this number can be written as

\[
d = 7^{a} \times 11^{b} \times 13^{c} \times 17^{e},
\]

where \(0 \le a, b, c, e \le 17\). We require \(d \equiv 5 \pmod{12}\).

Since \(13 \equiv 1 \pmod{12}\), we have \(13^{c} \equiv 1 \pmod{12}\) for any \(c\). Thus the condition reduces to

\[
7^{a} \times 11^{b} \times 17^{e} \equiv 5 \pmod{12}.
\]

Compute the residues modulo \(12\) for the powers:

- \(7^{a} \equiv \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } a \text{ even},\\ 7 & \text{if } a \text{ odd}. \end{cases}\)
- \(11^{b} \equiv \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } b \text{ even},\\ 11 & \text{if } b \text{ odd}. \end{cases}\)
- \(17^{e} \equiv \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } e \text{ even},\\ 5 & \text{if } e \text{ odd}. \end{cases}\)

Let the parities of \(a,b,e\) be denoted by \(x,y,z \in \{0,1\}\) where \(0\) means even and \(1\) means odd. Then the product modulo \(12\) is \(7^{x} \cdot 11^{y} \cdot 5^{z}\). Testing all eight possibilities:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(x,y,z) & \text{product} & \pmod{12} \\
\hline
(0,0,0) & 1 & 1 \\
(0,0,1) & 5 & 5 \\
(0,1,0) & 11 & 11 \\
(0,1,1) & 55 & 7 \\
(1,0,0) & 7 & 7 \\
(1,0,1) & 35 & 11 \\
(1,1,0) & 77 & 5 \\
(1,1,1) & 385 & 1
\end{array}
\]

The condition \( \equiv 5 \pmod{12}\) holds exactly for \((x,y,z) = (0,0,1)\) and \((1,1,0)\). That is:

- \(a\) even, \(b\) even, \(e\) odd; or
- \(a\) odd, \(b\) odd, \(e\) even.

Now count the number of choices for each exponent. Among the integers \(0\) through \(17\) inclusive, there are \(9\) even numbers and \(9\) odd numbers.

For the first pattern: \(9\) choices for \(a\) (even), \(9\) for \(b\) (even), \(9\) for \(e\) (odd) → \(9^3 = 729\) triples \((a,b,e)\).

For the second pattern: \(9\) for \(a\) (odd), \(9\) for \(b\) (odd), \(9\) for \(e\) (even) → another \(729\) triples.

Thus there are \(729 + 729 = 1458\) valid triples \((a,b,e)\).

The exponent \(c\) (for the factor \(13\)) is unrestricted and can be any of the \(18\) values \(0,1,\dots,17\). Hence the total number of divisors satisfying the condition is

\[
N = 1458 \times 18 = 26244.
\]

Finally, the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(1000\) is

\[
26244 \bmod 1000 = 244.
\]

Thus the answer is \(\boxed{244}\).
